name: Lankershim Blvd at Main St
approach: all approaches within 61 m x 91 m box

detection.rule: rear_end / lane_change: event while TTC <= 1.5 s for >= 0.3 s; crossing: PET <= 5.0 s over the shared swept-footprint zone
detection.citation: FHWA SSAM default (Gettman et al. 2008, FHWA-HRT-08-051; SSAM User Manual FHWA-HRT-08-050)

drac.rule: drac_flag = DRAC_max >= 3.4 m/s^2 (11.2 ft/s^2); reported alongside TTC events, not a detection criterion
drac.citation: AASHTO (2018) A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, 7th ed.

q_status.note: validation RMSE within 1% of optimum over this q range

repair.truth: Savitzky-Golay-smoothed NGSIM track (held out inside gaps); uniform protocol. See summary.protocols for the occluder protocol and raw-truth variant.

uniform.description: seeded random gaps 0.5-5.0 s, 1-2 per track, >= 1.0 s from track ends

q_status.note: validation RMSE within 1% of optimum over this q range
validation RMSE within 1% of optimum over this q range

occluder.description: real 2D line-of-sight occlusion intervals from a virtual roadside sensor; intervals 0.5-5.0 s kept, >= 1.0 s from track ends; visible flickers <= 2 frames merged

q_status.note: validation RMSE within 1% of optimum over this q range
validation RMSE within 1% of optimum over this q range

truth_variants.smoothed: Savitzky-Golay (15 frames, order 2) NGSIM positions as input and truth
truth_variants.raw: unsmoothed NGSIM local_x/local_y (ft->m) as input and truth; NGSIM-interpolated frames excluded from scoring

screening.rule: tracks with any 0.1 s displacement > 5 m (smoothed or raw) are not scored in either protocol (NGSIM position jumps); they still occlude others

notes: Truth 'smoothed' is the Savitzky-Golay (15 frames, order 2) track; the smoother also spreads information from inside a gap into its first/last ~0.7 s of context, which favours smooth models.

Truth 'raw' is the unsmoothed NGSIM position (ft->m); it carries NGSIM measurement noise, so it bounds achievable RMSE from below: Punzo, V., Borzacchiello, M. T., Ciuffo, B. (2011). On the assessment of vehicle trajectory data accuracy and application to the Next Generation SIMulation (NGSIM) program data. Transportation Research Part C 19(6), 1243-1262.

Reconstruction of noisy NGSIM trajectories and its validation: Montanino, M., Punzo, V. (2015). Trajectory data reconstruction and simulation-based validation against macroscopic traffic patterns. Transportation Research Part B 80, 82-106.

Occluder protocol is 2D (shadow of nearer vehicle footprints along the sensor ray, sensor height ignored): it over-states occlusion by cars relative to a 4.5 m pole and should be read as a realistic gap-placement protocol, not a LiDAR visibility model.
Speed is not scored against raw truth: differentiated raw NGSIM positions are dominated by jitter.

pedestrian_pet.rule: pedestrian footprint 0.5 x 0.5 m swept along its track while inside a crosswalk polygon; vehicle footprint as for crossing PET; zone = intersection of the two swept footprints; PET = t(second enters) - t(first leaves); detected at PET <= 5.0 s, any conflict angle; overlap (simultaneous occupancy) recorded with pet = 0
pedestrian_pet.note: study-specific severity bins (PET <= 1 s critical, <= 2 s serious, <= 5 s moderate); video-based VRU studies place conflict thresholds at 1-3 s (Zangenehpour et al. 2016); no FHWA/SSAM standard
pedestrian_pet.citation: Allen et al. (1978) TRR 667; Zangenehpour et al. (2016) AAP 86

failure_to_yield.rule: a vehicle's front enters a crosswalk polygon at t_v while a pedestrian is inside the same polygon, or within 3.0 s before the pedestrian enters it; the vehicle never slowed below 0.5 m/s (1.1 mph) in the 3.0 s before entry; and it had a stopping opportunity: its path distance to the crosswalk when the pedestrian entered (or 3.0 s before its own entry if the pedestrian came second) was at least the AASHTO stopping distance 2.5 s * v + v^2 / (2 * 3.4 m/s^2)
failure_to_yield.severity: study-specific bins: pedestrian already in the crosswalk -> distance from the vehicle's entry point to the pedestrian at entry <= 3.6 m (one lane) critical, <= 7.2 m serious, else moderate; pedestrian arriving after the vehicle -> lead time <= 1 s critical, <= 2 s serious, else moderate
failure_to_yield.note: indicator, not a citation: the roadway-half condition of §552.003(a) and signal phase are not applied; at a signalised site vehicles proceeding on green past a pedestrian crossing against the signal are counted
failure_to_yield.citation: Texas Transportation Code §552.003; Fitzpatrick et al. (2006) NCHRP Report 562 (yielding and opportunity); AASHTO (2018) stopping sight distance
